topic: How to Open a Brokerage Account
subtopic: FDIC Insurance for Bank Sweep Deposits
source_evidence: Cash swept into deposit accounts through a brokerage firm’s bank sweep program is covered by FDIC insurance up to the $250,000 limit per customer at each FDIC-Insured bank that participates in the bank sweep program.
answer: When opening a brokerage account, ask how its bank sweep program handles uninvested cash and which FDIC-insured banks participate. Cash swept into deposit accounts is covered up to $250,000 per customer at each participating insured bank. Cash above that limit at a bank is not protected by FDIC insurance. You can check the amount held in your sweep accounts on your brokerage statements or by contacting your brokerage firm.
